notes: T968 (is --max-wall actually enforced?): NO before this fix — answered and repaired. CAUSE (one line): T214 demoted --max-wall to a silent-child-only fallback — the wall check sat inside the `else` branch of the watchdog, reachable only when no [progress] line or agent-lane stdout/stderr byte had ever been seen, so a producing lane was exempt from its own declared budget FOREVER; nothing on any surface compared elapsed to wall_budget either. This reproduces the measured incident exactly: two lanes at 4h57m/4h53m against --max-wall 7200, both producing (10.9 MB / 5.6 MB transcripts), both carrying wall_budget: 7200 in their run records. THE RULING MADE (the brief demanded one, 'silently letting it run' being nobody's decision): --max-wall is an ABSOLUTE ceiling again — a lane still producing past its budget IS terminated, because the budget is the operator's declared cost control (every downstream surface assumes it holds), while stuck-detection remains the job of --progress-timeout and the liveness fuses (T214/T586/T634's real concern — killing correct long-running jobs by a stuck-detector guess — is untouched). Defence-in-depth surface: watch-fleet now compares elapsed against the launch run record's wall_budget and renders OVER-WALL(elapsed/budget) on any live row past its budget, so an over-budget lane is visible even if a future defect stops the kill again.
